First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6-2x}{2} & =\frac{6-x}{3} \\ (6-2x)\cdot 3 & =2\cdot (6-x)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(6-2x)\cdot 3 & =2\cdot (6-x) \\ 18-6x & =12-2x \\ 18-6x-18 & =12-2x-18 \\ -6x & =-2x-6 \\ -6x+2x & =-2x-6+2x \\ -4x & =-6 \\ \frac{-4x}{-4} & =\frac{-6}{-4} \\ x & =\frac{6}{4} \\ x & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
